# agent-runtime-governance

> Runtime governance specs for multi-agent AI operations: a red-line guard hook (PreToolUse, exit 0/2),
> a domain × autonomy-level permission matrix (🟢/🟡/🔴), and a structured dispatch template
> (trace_id, owner, depth ≤ 4, done criteria). Aligned with the LGD (Lifecycle Governance Doctrine).
> Code is pure Python stdlib — zero third-party packages, zero network egress.

## What this repo is

A self-published reference of the three runtime pieces we run in daily multi-agent operations to keep
autonomous agents inside explicit boundaries. It is norms + code, not a runnable application.

## Core files

- [README.md](README.md): project overview, quick start, self-test, license layering
- [README_EN.md](README_EN.md): English overview
- [code/redline_guard.py](code/redline_guard.py): PreToolUse red-line guard hook (Python stdlib)
- [docs/permission_matrix_v1.md](docs/permission_matrix_v1.md): domain × autonomy-level policy
- [docs/dispatch_template_v1.md](docs/dispatch_template_v1.md): structured handoff / dispatch template
- [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff): citation metadata (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22821834)
- [LICENSE](LICENSE): code license (Apache-2.0 for `code/`)

## Red-line classes the hook blocks

- R1 — destructive delete aimed at protected targets (recursive delete AND danger target co-occur)
- R2 — plaintext secrets in commands or files (matched values are never echoed)
- R3 — system-level damage (format / partition / wipe / registry-HKLM / shadow-delete patterns)
- R4 — pipe-to-shell remote execution (fetch-a-script-and-run-it patterns)
